title: feat(id-caps): several agents in one world under distinct roles
body: Fixes #8300 Before: the policy point held one agent's session. Nothing let a world host several agents at once under different roles, cap how many could hold a role, or show that one agent's actions stay out of another's. After: `id_caps::world_agents::WorldAgents` is a world's table of live agent sessions, one `PolicySession` per agent, keyed by (agent, role). A world may cap concurrent agents per role (`ConcurrencyCaps`). A join past the cap, a second join by the same agent, a grant for another world or a ceiling that does not cover this one is refused, never queued, and every join, refusal and leave is a presence event with its reason. Calls go only to the acting agent's own session, so one agent's refusal or park never touches another. A leave hands the ledger back, so a rejoin keeps its spend. How: tests cover concurrent agents under their own ceilings, refusal and park isolation, cap refusal with its audited reason and the slot freed by a leave, refused joins, rejoin spend, and an owner-side ceiling change reaching one agent only. title: id-pg: error mapping and grantee collapse for the Postgres HTTP adapter (#13762)
body: Fixes #13762 Before: id-pg could refuse a query before the network (`Refusal`), but nothing turned source outcomes into stable error codes. A 401, a 404, a 5xx, a deadline, a non-JSON 200 or a bad value had no defined error, and nothing stopped a grantee from seeing why a source refused. After: `Failure::to_error(audience)` maps every outcome to a stable `ErrorCode` from the design's §6.1 table. Refusals that depend only on query text (`query_shape_refused`, `limit_exceeded`) come through unchanged, as do load outcomes (`rate_limited`, `timeout`, `adapter_unavailable`). Anything that depends on the data or the grant collapses for a grantee to one `{"code":"not_available"}` body. That covers a 401 or 403, a 404, and any other 4xx, and the body is byte-identical to the pre-network body for an unlisted relation (§6.2). The owner sees `credential_unavailable` for a 401 or 403, with a short fixed diagnostic. - `classify_response(status, body_is_json)` makes a non-JSON 2xx an error, never an empty result (§9 invariant 8). - `type_mapping_failed` names the column and its declared type and never the value (§9 invariant 6). - Diagnostics are fixed strings plus at most a status number. No error carries the source's response text, a header, a value or the credential (§9 invariant 4). How: a new pure module, `src/error.rs`. The model tests are in `tests/error_mapping.rs`: the whole §6.1 table for both audiences, the unknown-versus-withheld identical-body check (the issue's done check), the collapse of every grant- or data-dependent outcome to one body, and an exhaustive pass over every non-2xx status. title: feat(id): login binding, ID-key challenges, OPAQUE and OIDC login (#13710 slices 1-3)
body:
Part of #13710.

Before: id had no way to tie a login account (an OIDC `(iss, sub)` or an OPAQUE password account) to a user's ID key, so a login could not prove or recover which key it belongs to.

After: id-core has the three building blocks the #5684 synthesis calls for, each tested against the #5885 invariants.

- `login_binding` (slice 1): the signed `id/login-binding/v1` statement linking an ID public key to a login account, with custody profile, recovery commitment and generation chain; a registry that enrols and updates bindings (current-key or recovery-threshold authority); and single-use, audience-bound ID-key challenges for login acceptance and device enrolment.
- `opaque_login` (slice 2): OPAQUE (RFC 9807, opaque-ke 4, Ristretto255 + Argon2) registration and login. The OPAQUE `export_key` wraps a random client-held ID key, so the server never holds a password-derived key. Wrong password and unknown account fail the same way.
- `oidc_login` (slice 3): PKCE S256, authorization URL and token request body, JWKS parsing (RSA and EC P-256), and strict ID-token validation (RS256/ES256 only, kid required, no `crit`, no duplicate JSON keys, iss/aud/azp/exp/iat/nonce/sub checks). A valid token yields only an account pointer, never key authority.

How: three new modules in `pkgs/id/crates/id-core`, plus a fixed RS256 test token signed offline with a throwaway key. New deps: `opaque-ke` 4.0.1, `rand_core` 0.6 and `sha2` 0.10 (for opaque-ke), and `ring` 0.17 (JWT signature checks). Not yet wired into server routes or the CLI; that is the next slice.

title: docs(id): physical erasure decision for redacted talk-page and changelog bodies (#14278)
body: Fixes #14278 Before: the #5834 talk-page and changelog record left open whether a redacted body may ever be physically destroyed, and how that squares with the retained body hash and the verifiable chain. After: a decision record answers all three questions the issue asks. Physical destruction is supported for body bytes only, on three triggers (legal erasure, the author's own request, unlawful content); community or owner takedown stays a tombstone. Attribution and the chain are never destroyed. How: `doc/2026-11-25T02-00-00Z_design_id14278_physical_erasure/` records the decision: - bodies are committed to with a salted commitment `H(domain_tag || salt || body)` kept in the chain, with salt and bytes stored outside it, so erasing bytes plus salt keeps invariant 3 (end-to-end verification) and refines invariant 4 (the redact entry keeps the commitment) without letting anyone confirm a guessed body; - a new attributed `erase` changelog event, valid only after a `redact`; - per-body encryption keys for backups (crypto-shredding) and erasure replay on restore; foreign peers get the `erase` as a request, and disclosure must not promise global deletion; - four implementation slices, the first folded into #14274 before its schema lands. body: Fixes #13918 Before: the ID web app showed the browser's own error page whenever its server was unreachable, even for pages the user had just read. With no network, the app opens and any page visited since the current build was installed reads as last rendered; an unvisited page shows a small offline page with a link home. The next navigation after reconnecting shows live data again. title: Queue labels: label add/remove history in the mirror plus a task label cache (#14170 Q5)
body:
Part of #14170 (slice Q5, both halves).

Before: the github-ci mirror kept only each issue's and PR's current label set, so nothing recorded when a label was added or removed, or by whom. Queue tasks carried no label set of their own, so `fleet queue list` could not answer "which tasks are on hold" without a client-side join per row.

After: every webhook delivery that changes an issue's or PR's labels writes one `github_label_history` row with the exact `added` and `removed` names, the resulting `label_set`, the action, the sender and `gh_updated_at`; first sight and the backfill script write a start row with the full set. On the queue side every task carries `labels` (the mirror's JSON array) and `labels_synced_at`, and `fleet queue list --label user/hold` or `--label 'user/*'` lists exactly the tasks whose issue holds that label. `fleet queue show` prints both fields so staleness is visible.

How:
- Projector (`pkgs/github-ci/worker`): `labelDiff`, `parseLabelSet`, `snapshotLabelHistory` and `labelStartStmt` in `mirror.ts`, guarded by the existing `versionAccepts` / `deletionBlocks` checks so stale or redelivered events write nothing. The history write is fail-open after the mirror batch, like Q7. `mirror.sql` + DDL add the table and a `(repo, number, id)` index; `scripts/backfill.ts` writes start and snapshot rows (`label_history_rows`).
- Broker (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue`): `tasks.labels TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` and `labels_synced_at` (schema + additive ALTER). `core::event` refreshes a task's cache from `github_mirror_issues` after every transition commits (enqueue, claim, park, block, complete, ...). `/sweep` runs an actionable-only label pass at most hourly (checkpoint `fleet-sweeper/labels_sync`); `/labels-sync` runs one on demand and `all: true` backfills every task. Every refresh is fail-open: the mirror never gates work (#8575). A task whose issue has no mirror row keeps `[]` and a NULL stamp, which reads as "never synced". `/list` takes `label` (exact name, or a prefix ending in `*`), and the rich row carries both columns.
- Not covered: the hosted TypeScript queue door (`pkgs/fleet/hosted-worker`) does not share these broker hooks, the same gap Q1's history has there.

Oracle tests: vitest "mirror label history (#14170 Q5)" (labeling, unlabeling, stale and duplicate deliveries, first sight, PRs, comment deliveries) and Rust `task_labels_tests` (enqueue copies the mirror set with a stamp; a mirror-only label change reaches the cache through the sweep with no queue write; `user/*` lists exactly the held set; the hourly gate; a missing mirror table never fails a transition or the sweep).

Evidence so far: Worker suite at d79e4af6 on a GitHub-hosted runner (node:24 container), `npm ci`, `tsc --noEmit`, esbuild bundle of the backfill script and vitest all passed: 7 files, 101 tests (run developing-today-forks/fleet 45526962421).

title: id-pg: endpoint registration and owner config for the Postgres HTTP adapter (#13758)
body: Fixes #13758 Before: the Postgres-over-HTTP adapter (design #5805) had a query translator and collection allowlists, but nothing checked an endpoint before use. A PostgREST endpoint that served extra schemas, or a credential whose role could write or call functions, would have been accepted as is. After: `id_pg::register(config, &probe)` is the only way to get a `RegisteredEndpoint` (and from it a `Translator`). It refuses an endpoint whose `db-schemas` lists anything besides the one exposed schema, and a role holding `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `EXECUTE` or any other privilege beyond `SELECT` on relations and `USAGE` on the schema. That is the issue's done check (design §4, §9 invariant 9). The owner config (`EndpointConfig`) is checked first and needs nothing from the network, so the transport (#13763) can call `validate()` before it sends a credential anywhere. The checks: - **Base URL:** `https` only, or plain `http` on a loopback host (`localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `[::1]`). No user info, query or fragment (§2, §9 invariant 4). - **Names:** the alias, the schema and every collection allowlist are validated with the existing `is_plain_identifier` / `CollectionAllowlist::validate`. - **Collections:** each must name the exposed schema, relations must be unique, and a row cap of 0 is refused. - **Credential:** `credential_ref` must be set, and no registration error ever includes it. - **Owner config:** deserializes with `deny_unknown_fields`, so a stray `password` field is an error. How: a new `src/registration.rs` module, which is pure. The live probe is plain data (`EndpointProbe { db_schemas, role_grants }`) that the transport slice fills. New enforcement tests are in `tests/registration.rs`. `serde_json` was added as a dev-dependency only. title: feat(id-core): immutable presentation asset references and part maps (#14731 slice 1)
body: Before: the #5970 user presentation assets design (§2, "Assets by ID") had no code. There was no way to name an asset revision, record which parts it declares, or say what happens when a filter targets a part that isn't there. Publishing new artwork creates the next revision with its declared parts, and an existing revision never changes. - `PresentationRef` `{asset, filters, parts}`, matching the record's JSON shape. Unknown fields are refused. - `resolve`, which uses exactly the named revision. On an unknown revision or an undeclared part it returns `StepDown` with the reason, instead of substituting another revision or applying the chain to the whole asset. Acceptance from the plan: - Replacing artwork creates a new revision while an existing reference keeps rendering the old one: `replacing_artwork_creates_a_revision_and_old_references_keep_theirs`. - A chain on an undeclared part steps down a rung: `undeclared_part_steps_down_instead_of_applying_to_the_whole_asset`. title: feat(id-worlds): appeals against logged moderation actions
body:
Fixes #14467

Before: a moderation action could be reported, reviewed and shown in the transparency log, but nobody affected by it had a way to contest it.

After: `id_worlds::safety_appeal` lets an affected party file a signed appeal naming the contested action by the action hash the transparency view gives it. The appeal enters the review queue as its own item (`ReviewQueue::rebuild_with_appeals`) and a moderator decides it with the same signed closure through the same `ClosureLog::close`, so the decision lands in the same log and shows in the transparency view as an appeal decision. Deciding an appeal reverses nothing; a reversal stays a separate moderator action.

How: open question 1 of the outline is settled as it recommends, by content hash. Who counts as affected is the caller's `AppealStanding`, the same way the read path and moderator set are the caller's. One appellant has at most one open appeal per action. `ClosureLog::close` now takes any `QueueItems` (reports, appeals, or both). Also clears the clippy notes in `safety_review_queue`.

Tests run remotely with `--features sandbox`.

title: feat(fleet-queue): priority profile, dimensions and triage mechanics (PRI-01, PRI-02, PRI-05a-d)
body:
Before: the queue had no versioned priority profile. Ratified #7030 bands (expedite=15, next-up=25) lived only as constants, nothing typed rejected off-profile values instead of snapping them, there was no shared total candidate order or protected-owner priority gate, no evidence-based aging model, no temporary opportunity boost, no hysteresis, and no bounded clump refinement.

After: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/work/priority.rs` defines:
- PRI-01: `fleet.priority-profile/v1` with the queue profile (scale plus the exact 15/25 bands with evidence refs), named-intent cross-profile mappings with no arithmetic fallback, the V2 comparator (urgency, peer rank with legacy None as 0, creation time, canonical identity), and `check_priority_write`, the protected-owner gate (`OWNER_POLICY_PROTECTED`, `OWNER_POLICY_VERSION_CONFLICT`, fail closed when the policy or membership snapshot is missing).
- PRI-05a: `evaluate_aging`, which turns dated evidence into at most one scale step per sweep as an `aging_reconsideration` hint. Age alone only makes an item due; raising into Critical needs deadline evidence; protected expedite items are held; replayed, stale and future evidence is ignored.
- PRI-05b: `OpportunityBoost` (start, expiry, `expiry_action=retriage`), `effective_priority` and `evaluate_boost_expiry`. A boost changes only the effective value (strongest active boost, no stacking, never Critical, never on ratified bands or the protected set); expiry removes only the boost and returns an `opportunity_expired` retriage request carrying the unchanged base, so the item stays in the ordered backlog.
- PRI-05c: `HysteresisPolicy` and `evaluate_hysteresis`. Automatic moves must be one scale step, meet the confidence threshold, sit outside the cooldown since the item's last applied move (manual included), and stay within the net drift bound in the window; otherwise a `hysteresis_suppressed` hint with a retry time. Authorised manual/owner moves and verified deadline/incident evidence bypass the resistance, never the `priority.write` capability check or the protected-owner gate.
- PRI-05d: `ClumpPolicy` and `refine_clump`. One sweep over one equal-urgency clump turns comparisons (much/slightly more or less urgent, roughly equal, custom, needs research) into peer-rank moves relative to the reference: at most one move per item, a per-sweep cap, deterministic judgement order, and each move cites evidence, comparison, sweep and policy version. Protected items are held; replayed sweeps, mixed clumps and stale owner policy are refused.
- PRI-02: `explain_priority` and `PriorityExplanation` (`fleet.priority-explanation/v1`). Intrinsic urgency, nullable importance and the effective value are reported side by side against pinned inputs (profile, policies, snapshot, work version, time). Untriaged stays untriaged, null importance stays null and is never derived from urgency, legacy stored values read exactly, and mismatched or uncited inputs are `stale_snapshot`.

Remote test run (GitHub-hosted, head 374d1cd4): all 13 `pmo_priority_*` tests listed by exact name and passing; `work::` 81 passed, 0 failed.

How: pure module over the existing DST-01 `contracts.rs` types; no I/O, schema or live queue change. Named tests: `pmo_priority_profile_preserves_ratified_values`, `pmo_priority_profile_preserves_protected_expedite_membership`, `pmo_priority_aging_moves_both_directions_with_evidence`, `pmo_priority_aging_skips_protected_expedite_set`, `pmo_priority_opportunity_expiry_retriages_without_base_mutation`, `pmo_priority_opportunity_expiry_never_changes_protected_expedite`, `pmo_priority_hysteresis_cooldown_bounded_with_authorized_bypass`, `pmo_priority_hysteresis_cannot_bypass_owner_policy`, `pmo_priority_clump_sweep_caps_one_move_and_records_evidence`, `pmo_priority_clump_never_moves_protected_expedite`, `pmo_priority_dimensions_pin_explanation`, plus comparator and malformed-document tests. The TS half of PRI-01 (lossless 15/25 in `pm-stack/dispatch/src/validate.ts`) already landed via DST-02 (#9452). Built under Drew's 2026-11-24 ruling voiding self-imposed design-only gates.

title: docs(design): refusal-triggered failover lane sketch (#14234)
body: Before: #3150's acceptance criterion 3, the design for what a request does after the seated models refuse it on content-policy grounds, had no artifact. Its triage notes also described the router as having no content-policy class at all. After: `doc/2026-11-25T01-55-00Z_design_refusal-failover-lane-14234/` records the sketch, and it is grounded in what the fork does today. The fork already classifies refusals as `ContentPolicy`, keeps them out of route health (#1084), and fails a refused request over within its pool. The only gap is what happens when every seated candidate refuses. The sketch covers four things: - **Trigger:** the existing `ContentPolicy` class, used only when the refusals are unanimous across at least two provider families. - **Failover:** a dedicated route head that only the policy-exhaustion branch can reach. It is tried once per request, needs no output started, keeps state intact, enforces a tool-capability floor, and is off by default. - **Telemetry:** a `trigger` field and a `failover_from` field, health isolation in both directions, and no body capture. - **Bounds:** lawful use only, privacy terms, an outbound credential gate, a benchmark plan for Abliteration large-flash and Venice Uncensored 1.2, and a named pilot-approval gate. title: fix(pm-stack): dispatch, exporters and claimant install follow the home-resolution contract (#8220 slice 3)
body: Before: 12 defaults outside the aggregator still called `os.homedir()`, which silently falls back to the passwd entry when HOME is unset or empty: the dispatch config and its fleet binary path, the quota watchdog, the opencode usage, meta and cloudflare exporters, and the claimant installer. After: none is left anywhere in pm-stack. An unset or empty HOME is a named error that says which setting or flag avoids it, a set HOME gives exactly the same paths as before, and an explicit override never needs HOME. Each tool fails the way it already fails for bad input: - **dispatch:** `HomeUnresolvedError` from config, through a dispatch copy of the aggregator's `requireHome`; the fleet binary path resolves at spawn time, so only the gh fallback that needs it fails. - **quota watchdog:** defaults are lazy; the flags and `QUOTA_WATCHDOG_ADAPTERS_DIR` need no HOME. - **opencode usage export:** a missing HOME fails the tick as `read-failed` with its failure document where one can be written, instead of throwing; `--out-dir` plus `OPENCODE_USAGE_DB` need no HOME. - **meta and cloudflare exporters:** no HOME with no `--out-dir` is a usage error (exit 2, nothing written). - **claimant install:** the default store is resolved only when `--store` is absent; no HOME is a usage error naming `--store`. How: a probe test per suite covers HOME set, unset and blank, and the override paths. Slices 1 (#14741) and 2 (#14746) covered the aggregator. The quota watchdog's own `watchdog.test.ts` is not run by any workflow, so its change has no new test here. title: feat(id-worlds): moderator review queue over safety reports
body:
Fixes #14465

Before: safety reports could be filed (#14464), but moderators had no ordered view of what is open, and no record of how a report was closed.

After: `id_worlds::safety_review_queue` rebuilds a review queue from the report log and a closure log. Open reports sort by a configurable reason order (abuse, impersonation, spam, other by default), then by filing time. A moderator closes a report with a signed closure (actioned, no action, or duplicate) that lands in an append-only `closures.jsonl`.

How: `Closure` and `SignedClosure` use the same signing scheme as reports, under their own domain separator. `ClosureLog::close` checks the signature, that the signer is a moderator, that the report exists, and that it is not already closed. `ReviewQueue::rebuild` is a pure projection, so it can be rebuilt any time from the two logs.

title: feat(id-worlds): signed safety report facts with operator-scoped intake (#14464)
body: Before: There was no way to file a safety report against a public world or program. The v3 safety outline (#6310) names a report fact as the first slice, and the review queue (#14465) and appeals (#14467) both wait on its shape. After: `id-worlds` has a `safety_report` module. A report is a signed, timestamped fact naming the target, a reason class (spam, abuse, impersonation, other) and the reporter. An operator's intake accepts it only when the target is something that operator lists or hosts: a program its gallery lists, a world it hosts, or a program version a hosted world has recorded as published (the #13742 fact). Accepted reports append to a `reports.jsonl` log under the operator directory, and the log re-verifies every line when it loads. Filing a report changes nothing about the target. How: `SignedReport` follows the `SignedCollection` pattern (exact JSON signed with a domain separator over its BLAKE3), and the report id is the BLAKE3 of the signed document, so filing the same report twice appends nothing. Scope is a small `OperatorScope` trait, implemented by `Gallery` (via a new `Gallery::lists`), by `HostedScope` (built from each hosted world's records), and by a pair of scopes so an operator running both is covered. Intake also refuses a filing time more than five minutes ahead of the node's clock. Stacked on #14606 (the #13742 draft/published fact). Merge that first; this PR's diff against main then shrinks to its own three files. Tests: 12 new unit tests in `safety_report` (signature and tamper refusal, bounds, gallery-listed accept/refuse, hosted world and published-only program scope, combined scope, future timestamp, target unchanged, append/dedupe/reload, tampered log refused, reason names). Verified by remote dispatch; results recorded on #14464. Fixes #14464 --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_ --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? body: Closes #10271 (slice A9115-privacy-filter). ## What New `location_policy` module for id-store: scope authorization applied **before** location candidate counts and projection, per the #9115 privacy rule ("queries filter authorization before ranking or returning candidate counts; public enumeration is prohibited unless explicitly configured"). - `ScopeAuthorization` — the caller's authenticated namespace + tenant scope (#9083 context, consumed not defined), plus two explicitly configured grants: public visibility and unverified visibility. - Visibility: `Public` entries need the public grant or the scope grant; `Scope` entries need the exact scope; `StoredUnverified` entries need the scope **and** the unverified grant (a `stored_unverified` observation is never proof of content, A-9115.1); tombstone-created entries (no access class) are scope-private. - `AuthorizedLocations` view: `candidate_count`, `candidates`, `entry`, `visible_len`, `projection` (the materialized subset ranking/caching may hold), and A-9115.1 acknowledgements — `VerifiedPresent` / `NotPresent` / `Indeterminate` internally, coalesced `ExternalAck` externally. Every output is a function of the authorized visible subset only: an unauthorized location is indistinguishable from an absent one, so counts cannot leak unauthorized existence. - Authorization filters visibility only, never states: visible entries keep state, provenance and lineage (A-9115.2). title: fix(pm-console): the edge could not make a request of its own: no notification it sent ever left
body: **No notification the edge has sent ever left it.** Nor did it ever read the Android release from GitHub. Both failed the same way, silently, since the edge first went in front of the site (b7b881dc37, 2026-11-22 11:14Z). ## What was wrong In the Worker runtime the platform's `fetch` refuses to be called as a method of another object. `this.fetchImpl(url)`, with the global `fetch` kept in `fetchImpl`, throws: ``` TypeError: Illegal invocation: function called with incorrect `this` reference. ``` bun and Node do not mind, so every test passed. The edge kept the global `fetch` on itself and called it exactly that way: | Where | What it broke | | --- | --- | | the sender of notifications | every notification from the edge: a reply from the fleet, something that needs the owner, a unit that keeps failing, the laptop gone quiet. The failure was caught, counted, and shown nowhere | | the Android release | the edge never knew of a release; a download always fell back to the laptop's copy | | the laptop's own classes, run at the edge | every read and write of the queue store in direct mode, had it been switched on | ## How it was found Health had just been made to say which release the edge knows of (#12946). On the deployed Worker it said none, while the release was plainly published. Reproduced in the runtime itself: called as a method, `fetch` throws; called plainly, it works. ## The fix, and why it cannot come back quietly - No class keeps a `fetch` it was given: each keeps a plain caller (`src/plain.ts`). - **The tests can now see it.** The stand-in `fetch` handed to the edge, to direct mode and to `Ops` refuses to be called as a method, as the runtime's does. With the code as it was, **21 tests fail** on it (the release, the notifications, direct mode); with the fix they pass. - **The deploy checks it in the real runtime.** The run of the bundle in the Worker runtime now checks that the state can make a request of its own. Run here with the fix, it reads the real release from GitHub (`2026.11.23-0f311ae`); with the fix taken out it fails, quoting the runtime. - Health says why the release could not be read (`androidReleaseTrouble`), so "none published" and "could not ask" no longer look the same from outside. ## Checked `bun test` 194 pass; five planted faults each caught (a sixth was in a line that turned out to be redundant, which is removed); the real-runtime run passes with the fix and fails without it. ## Not checked A notification leaving the deployed Worker: that needs a subscribed device. What I check after the deploy is that the deployed Worker now reads the release, which is the same `fetch`. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_ --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? title: Console surface for bridge wake-hook management (#14544)
body: ## Wake-hook management in the PM Stack console Implements #14544 (follow-up to bridge S12, #14378): retiring the standalone bridge page removed its wake-hook form; wake hooks had no console surface. title: fleet-brokers: cap TCP per-request worker concurrency (#14330)
body: ## Summary Fixes #14330 (remainder of darwin-nix#1925). Both broker TCP accept loops spawned one thread per request with no cap, and the request-level limiter could not safely shed load: at saturation `req.respond`/`drop` drained unread Content-Length bodies under tiny_http and stalled the accept loop. - New shared `tcp_http::serve` (used by both `queue_broker` and `secrets_broker` TCP loops): admission happens on the raw socket, before parsing or spawning. Past `MAX_CONNECTIONS` (128) the socket closes immediately — no response write, no body drain, no worker thread, no retained Request (UDS-style shed, same cap as the UDS loop via shared `InFlightSlot`). - Framing is the hardened `uds_http` parser generalized to `Read`/`Write` (`read_tcp_head`): request-line validation, duplicate/conflicting/unparsable Content-Length rejection, pre-body auth/size gate identical to UDS. Chunked bodies and `Expect: 100-continue` from the tiny_http surface are retained; chunked-oversize 413 keeps the prior adapter's `{}` body. - `tiny_http` dependency removed in favor of `chunked_transfer`. ## Tests - New burst regression `unauthenticated_withheld_body_burst_is_bounded_and_recovers`: holds 128 unauthenticated withheld-body peers, asserts all 32 overload sockets close with zero response bytes and only 128 precheck entries, then a healthy request completes while rejected peers are still held. - New `chunked_expect_and_oversize_parity`: chunked decode, `100-continue`, oversize 413. - Remote run `developing-today-forks/fleet#45512186076` (`cd pkgs/fleet && cargo test -p fleet-queue --features queue-broker,secrets-broker`): **700 passed, 0 failed** (691 lib, incl. the new tests). - Independent review findings fixed: 413 body parity and zero-byte shed assertion. title: fix(id/bridge): budget the encoded batch size in every sender (#14644)
body: Closes #14644 ## Problem Bridge senders budgeted only event payload bytes, while receivers enforce `maxBatchBytes` against the encoded batch — 4-byte count plus a 4-byte length per event. Honest peers could emit a batch their peer was bound to reject (at default limits, 16 × 64 KiB events formed one 1,048,644-byte batch over the 1,048,576-byte bound), and retrying the unchanged transfer repeated the failure. ## Fix All senders now budget the encoded size `4 + Σ(4 + event.length)` and split before the first event that would cross the bound: - **Hosted server + reference client** (`pkgs/id/hosted-worker/src/bridge-session.ts`): new exported `encodedEventBytes` / `encodedBatchBytes` / `splitBatches`; both senders split through `splitBatches`, so the accounting exists exactly once. An event that cannot fit any batch under the session limits fails the server session with the named `event_too_large` error; the client throws the same named message. - **Hosted HTTP pull** (`pkgs/id/hosted-worker/src/user-do.ts`): budgets the framed size; a first event that cannot fit any batch is a named 413 `event_too_large` refusal rather than an empty batch with `x-bridge-more: 1` that the caller would retry forever. - **Native WebSocket sender** (`pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/bridge.rs`): same accounting in `send_batches`; an unfittable event is a named error. - **Native HTTP pull mirror** (`pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/bridge_http.rs`): the in-crate mirror of the hosted pull repeats the same accounting and 413 refusal (found during the fix; same defect shape). The mirror gains a `limits` field so tests can drive non-default bounds. The native HTTP push client already checked the encoded body and is unchanged. ## Verification Route note: the Actions exec runner cannot check out an unmerged branch and has no Node, so — as with the sibling hosted-worker lanes — the suites ran in the laptop worktree `~/wt-lane-iw241-14644`; CI on main re-verifies after merge. - The issue's own reproduction, re-run against the fixed code: `batchCount: 2, batchEvents: [15, 1]` and every batch accepted by `decodeBatch` under the same limits (previously one 1,048,644-byte batch, refused). - `pkgs/id/hosted-worker`: full suite **222/222 pass** (`node --experimental-transform-types --test`, all files in the package test script), `tsc --noEmit` clean. New tests: `splitBatches` exact-fit / first-overflow / count-bound / cannot-fit, the default-limit 16 × 64 KiB split, a 200-trial property test (every emitted batch decodes under the same limits, sequence preserved), tight-limit session convergence in both directions (only the encoded size separates the batches), both cannot-fit session failures by name, and a DO pull test paging 64 × 16,384-byte checkpoint events at [63, 1]. (Signed events cannot be padded to exactly 64 KiB — event-tree byte strings cap at 512 and extension keys are a closed set — so the 64 KiB default-limit case is covered at the sender level on raw bytes, exactly as the issue's reproduction drove it, and the DO pull uses checkpoint events padded to an exact 16,384 bytes.) - `pkgs/id` (from the workspace root): `cargo test -p id-sync` — **261 passed, 1 failed**. title: fix(fleet-queue): lease-expiry diagnostic names heartbeat only, not checkpoint (#14653)
body: Closes #14653. ## Problem The lease-expiry diagnostic in `not_claimed_reason` told a worker whose lease had lapsed to use "heartbeat or checkpoint to keep a lease". But `verb_checkpoint` writes a checkpoint KV, task progress/`updated_at`, worker activity and an event only — it never advances `lease_until`. A worker following the advertised guidance could save progress successfully and still lose the claim at the original deadline. ## Changes - **Rust broker** (`turso_queue/lifecycle.rs`): the diagnostic now reads "heartbeat to keep a lease; checkpoint saves progress but does not renew it". - **Hosted-worker mirror** (`hosted-worker/src/queue.ts`): the identical `notClaimedReason` text gets the identical fix, so both doors give the same guidance. - **Agent-next guidance** (`fleet-agent/src/next.rs`): the queue-rung hand-out now names heartbeat for long work ("On long work, heartbeat to extend the lease; title: fix(fleet-agent): priority reservations remove the shortlist row
body: Closes #14651 ## The defect `shortlist::reserve` recorded a priority hand-out in `handed` but left a matching pre-existing shortlist row in `entries`, and `Shortlist::take` never checked `recently_handed`. Reachable sequence: issue X is shortlisted; agent A reserves X through the priority rung (`next --no-shortlist`); agent B then takes the still-listed X row before GitHub state changes. Both get the same issue — the file lock serializes the operations but cannot prevent the sequential duplicate. ## The fix (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-agent/src/shortlist.rs`) - New `Shortlist::reserve_from`, the in-memory core of `reserve`: a reservation now also removes any shortlist row for the same repo/issue, atomically inside the same locked update that records the hand-out. - `Shortlist::take` defensively skips entries already handed out within the TTL, so a stale row written before this fix (or restored from an old file) cannot resurrect the issue. The row becomes eligible again once the hand-out ages out of the window. ## Tests - `a_priority_reservation_removes_the_shortlist_row_for_the_same_issue` — the reported sequence end to end at the file level (seed → reserve → take gives the *other* entry; a further take finds nothing). - `take_never_hands_out_an_issue_already_handed_within_the_window` — a listed-but-handed row is skipped until the TTL passes. - `mixed_handouts_never_repeat_an_issue` — property test: arbitrary add/take/reserve interleavings hand each issue out at most once within the window. title: fix(id-caps): stale QuotaLedgerStore close cannot clear a newer checkout
body: Closes #14602. ## What Per-pair checkout epochs on `QuotaLedgerStore`: each `open` stamps the handle with the pair's next epoch, and `close` ignores a ledger whose epoch does not match the live checkout. A `release` called while the handle is still live still admits a second open (the store cannot tell live from dropped), but the older handle's later close is now stale and ignored instead of clearing the live checkout and writing its older ledger back over the newer spend. `restore` reseeds each pair's next epoch past its snapshot so a pre-restart handle's late close is stale too. `checkout_epoch` is `#[serde(default)]`, so pre-change snapshots still load. ## Evidence - Reproduced the exact #14602 sequence first (open A → release while live → open/charge B → close A): stale close cleared B's checkout and B's spend was lost. After the fix the same sequence keeps B checked out with its spend intact. - New regression tests: `store_release_of_a_live_handle_cannot_lose_a_newer_handles_spend`, `restored_store_ignores_a_pre_restart_handles_late_close`. - `cargo test -p id-caps` (manifest path): 307 passed, 0 failed; clippy clean; rustfmt applied. - Genuinely-dropped recovery (#14580) preserved: existing release tests unchanged and green. ```json { "direct_parent": null, "links": [], "lineage": { "design": null, "roadmap_item": null, "priority": null }, "pm_meta": 1, "provenance": { "queue_id": null, "scheduled_start": null, "picked_up_at": null, "work_started_at": null, "created_at": "2026-11-24T21:57:41Z", "session_id": "ses_e5df0ed5bdbffeJsUBhM5OlY8f", "lane": null, "host": "amd", "worktree": "/home/user/git/wt-code-j-14602", "model": null, "lane_start_issues": [], "workspace_ref": { "kind": "worktree", "id": "/home/user/git/wt-code-j-14602", "repo": "developing-today/code", "branch": "lane/code-j/14602-verify", "sha": "25e275dda51413417dea729d2665fa956f5fbe84" }, "auth_subject": "agent-next-25-local", "stamped_by": "fleet 0.1.0 (native)" } } ``` --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR?
